sourceBindings.text: Operate only under the matched manual and trainer, but never touch, clean, adjust or diagnose moving tines while the engine runs. For care, stop normally or in an emergency as the manual requires, wait for complete movement to cease and for hot engine/exhaust parts to cool, turn the fuel valve off when applicable, and follow the actual manual's anti-start procedure. For the documented SER rotary-tine inspection, Honda printed p. 52 requires engine off, spark-plug cap disconnected, fuel valve off, level immobilized machine and heavy gloves. Do not inhale fuel vapour or refuel around heat/flames. Refuel outdoors only, with the engine stopped and allowed to cool, away from flames, sparks and smoking. Follow the manual's spill and vapour precautions before any start; no cooling duration is supplied here.

A real loose bolt, missing guard, fuel leak or abnormal vibration is a stop condition. The source's planned loosened-handlebar fault belongs on a photograph or inert disabled demonstrator, never on a machine that might run. Likewise, a trainer explains physical control on a stopped isolated machine rather than using two people on powered handlebars.

sourceBindings.text: Permitted learner exterior/rotor care needs stopped, isolated, secure equipment and enough cooling to prevent burns. This is not a rule that all maintenance requires a fully cold engine: the qualified Honda oil-change procedure specifies a warm stopped engine. Oil changes, plug adjustment, fuel draining and belt work are not default learner tasks. Never apply oil or cleaner liquid to the documented clutch lever, lock lever or lock arm. Used oil goes to appropriate collection, not soil or ordinary trash.

sourceBindings.text: After safe stop, isolation and cooling, remove accessible caked-on soil, crop debris and stones from the exterior and, where the manual permits, rotary area using the prescribed tool and gloves. Check guards, visibly loose fasteners, cable/control damage and tine wear or bends. Report defects; do not restart to see whether a suspected fault disappears. A learner may carry out only the tasks for which the trainer and actual manual have qualified them. Tine replacement, oil changes, plug adjustment, fuel-system draining or belt work are not default student tasks.

sourceBindings.text: The original practical card asks for air-cleaner removal, cleaning and reseating. For the Honda example, printed p. 18 specifies inspection and cleaning if necessary. Service pp. 43–44 distinguish foam from paper: foam is cleaned by the prescribed method, dried thoroughly, dipped in clean engine oil and squeezed to remove excess without twisting; paper is lightly tapped or air-blown from inside out, never brushed, and replaced if excessively dirty. These are model-specific learning points, not permission for an untrained learner to service an unknown device. Never use gasoline or low-flash-point solvents or run the engine without the air cleaner; reinstall the elements and cover correctly by the actual manual. Record a check truthfully without claiming full service was required or performed every time.

sourceBindings.text: Record operation hours and the last service. Honda printed pp. 40–41 specify after-storage, each-use, first-month/20-hour, three-month/50-hour, six-month/100-hour and yearly/300-hour columns as applicable; where a calendar and hour interval share a column, use whichever comes first. Dusty use can require more frequent air-cleaner attention. The source's 'grease bearing seats weekly' is not an FJ500-SER maintenance rule; the SER table places grease application in the **after-storage** column and marks it for dealer service. The yearly/300-hour column applies to other listed tasks, not this grease row. Engine oil, transmission oil, spark plug, belt and cable tasks each have their own intervals and qualification. A learner reports due work and the trainer assigns a qualified person instead of improvising it.

sourceBindings.text: For transport or long storage, Honda printed pp. 61–63 call for the fuel valve off and upright/level handling to avoid spills; extended storage involves a dry clean location and a model-specific fuel-draining procedure. Fuel handling is for a competent adult using the manual and local controls, not an unsupervised student. Protect exposed damage from corrosion only with an approved maintenance method, and record tine wear, paint damage and storage conditions. A dry indoor place alone is not the whole storage procedure.

sourceBindings.text: The teacher's scenario says a full tank and sputtering engine mean the air filter is the next thing to check. A dirty or badly seated filter can affect running, and the original bank MCQ asks for it; preserve that candidate. But a full tank does not prove that fuel reaches the engine, that the fuel valve or switch is on, that the plug works, or that the air cleaner is the single next check. The documented Honda no-start chart, printed p. 64, asks about fuel amount, fuel-valve position, engine-switch position, carburetor fuel supply and plug condition, then directs unresolved failure to the dealer. The actual machine's symptom and manual determine order. Stop the engine, avoid spills/hot parts, and let a competent person perform hazardous fuel or ignition checks.

The source's universal 'no more than two continuous hours' is not established by the FJ500-SER manual. Monitor heat, fatigue, abnormal sound and ventilation; schedule safe breaks by conditions and the actual manual. Never run a malfunctioning machine simply to reproduce a fault for a class. Never run a gasoline engine in an enclosed or partially enclosed space, or near open windows or doors where exhaust can enter. A fan or ventilation proposal does not override that carbon-monoxide boundary.

sourceBindings.text: For ineffective weed removal, retain the source's plausible candidates: worn or dull tines, a pass that is too quick for engagement, and soil that is too hard or wet. For difficult handling, consider obstacles, an uneven pull, wrong setting or loose connections. Do not assume one cause from the visible result. Stop safely before inspecting and preserve crops and ground conditions. A badly worn tine or fastener is for a qualified person to correct. Do not manually test a moving tine, belt or connection.

Excessive vibration is an immediate stop, not a challenge to keep cultivating. After shutdown, isolation and cooling, inspect only within the trainee's authorized scope for loose parts or damaged/bent tines; refer possible engine/drive imbalance to the qualified technician. The original scenario's two plausible causes are not a definitive diagnosis. One eligible learner controls a real machine at a time and each person's performance is recorded separately.

sourceBindings.text: The original workshop labels its phases: safety/identification 5 minutes, pre-use/start 10, a 30 m pass/evaluation 15 and stop/clean/report 10. Those labels total 40 minutes, and the 15-minute field phase already includes discussion. The table separately lists 35 minutes work plus 10 discussion; their overlap is not explained. If the ten discussion minutes are additional, the phase plan would be 50 minutes before extra individual turns, but this is not a proven source minimum. Plan enough time for every output and each learner's safe observed turn; never compress isolation or care to fit the table. Record actual machine, operator, date and operating-hour record, checks, abnormal findings, corrective action/referral and trainer observation/signature. Naming three pre-checks on the source exit ticket checks recall, not observed post-use care.

The final teacher self-assessment table on physical p. 217 lists other soil/crop outcomes but omits this cultivator task. Add a learner reflection on safe shutdown, permitted cleaning, fault reporting and what still needs practice. Mark 'can / partly / cannot' honestly. Self-rating helps plan learning; it never awards an observed practical pass. If no eligible machine/learner/site is available, keep practical C01 unattempted and use case analysis for C02/C03 only.

Continue the shared workshop’s preparation and rotating roles from S3-14 with clear commands, pictorial checklists and safe inert demonstrations. Keep one instructed eligible operator and each learner’s own evidence. Afterward discuss a key takeaway and three pre-checks actually performed, without inventing experience. Corrosion prevention and extended storage use an approved compatible method and qualified manual procedure.
Use this self-reflection to identify what you can do and what needs more practice. It does not record a practical result or replace the trainer’s observation.
